newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom jumbo bond highlight of Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom jumbo bond highlight of Eurobonds.

text.p: A $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond from British Telecommunications Plc was the market's main focus on Tuesday, attracting investors because of the rarity appeal of the borrower and the generous pricing of its bond.
"The deal has been very well-handled, and has been well-received by investors," a syndicate manager at a bank involved in the transaction said.
Officials at joint lead manager Merrill Lynch and SBC Warburg said the deal was a "blow-out".

The bond was priced to yield 15 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. By 1610 GMT the deal had tightened by half a notch, and traders said the yield pick-up was likely to narrow further over time as the bonds were placed with retail investors.
BT's treasurer told Reuters the decision to tap the markets was driven by its need for funds ahead of the multi-billion dollar merger with MCI Communications Corp.
He said BT had to make a cash payment to MCI shareholders in the region of $2.5 billion in September.
Eurobond traders expressed some surprise at BT's decision to pay up to tap the market because it is a cash-rich institution.
"BT's funding target is known to be 25 b.p. below Libor, and today's deal gives them funds at around 8 b.p. below," a trader at a U.S. bank said.
"BT is very cash-rich, so some people are wondering if BT is planning something which is not yet known about which will require funding in the future," he said.

On the emerging markets side, Turkey was due to hold the London leg of its roadshow on Wednesday. It plans to issue a $250 million five-year bond via J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg. Spread talk was around 275 b.p. over Treasuries.
After tapping the yen bond market on Tuesday, Mexico was expected to issue a 500 billion lire 20-year bond next week via lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
